text: In a native Salesforce dashboard, the author sets a filter and viewers change it. CRM Analytics dashboards go much further. A click on one widget can reshape every other widget, and a row can lead straight into a Salesforce record. This lesson covers how.

Start with faceting. Here, one Opportunity Owner selector is set to a single person, and the chart and the key metric numbers narrow to match. Nobody edited a query. Faceting works because those widgets share a dataset. Selections on charts, dates, lists, ranges, and toggles filter their neighbors automatically.

Each widget's query panel holds the switches. Faceting controls how the widget reacts to other selections. Apply global filters decides whether it respects dashboard-wide filters. And Broadcast selections as facets decides whether a click here filters everything else. Check the current docs for the exact options in your release.

So there are three layers. Faceting is automatic and needs no code. Selection interactions, meaning bindings, let one query change part of another, even across datasets. And actions take the viewer somewhere else, such as a record or a global action. Start with faceting, and reach for bindings only when it can't express what you need.

When a widget won't respond, work through a short checklist. Do the widgets share a dataset? Is broadcast on for the source? Is faceting on the target set to something other than None? Is a global filter or initial selection quietly narrowing results?
Next up: performance tuning, because every interaction you add is another query the dashboard has to run.
